title.narrative: Envelope 3: Contingency Plan for Rapid response for Displacement and Return

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtBuilding on its extensive experience in rapid emergency response, Violet Organization (VO) is proposing a 12-month adaptable project aimed at scaling up its capacity and strengthening its emergency preparedness for swift and effective responses to displacement and return scenarios.ltbrgtThe project aims to ensure that Violet can deliver timely and appropriate assistance within 48 hours of a crisis onset, whether triggered by renewed hostilities, rising insecurity, harsh winter conditions, or environmental stressors such as floods, heavy snowfall, or rainfall, as well as other events leading to displacement or return.ltbrgtTo achieve this, Violet will maintain a high level of operational readiness, including strong communication and coordination with stakeholders across Syria. The organization will establish clear indicators for potential triggers and monitor them closely. Violet’s Safety and Security and MEAL teams will take a proactive role in tracking field conditions and identifying early warning signs. In parallel, Violet will leverage its extensive volunteer network and community acceptance to support early warning mechanisms and enable rapid mobilization. Additionally, Violet will promote the use of feedback mechanisms, allowing communities to report incidents that may lead to displacement or return.ltbrgtAs part of the initial response strategy, Violet proposes a multi-sectoral lifesaving package that includes one-off Emergency Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC), Non-Food Item (NFI) kits, winterization cash support, and emergency food assistance through ready-to-eat rations, as well as protection intervention including Awareness-Raising Campaigns to inform affected communities and returnees about their rights, available services, and protection risks, case management and PSS.ltbrgtThe cash modality is based on recent assessments indicating strong beneficiary preference. This method upholds the dignity of recipients, speeds up response, and gives households the flexibility to meet their most urgent needs. It is also expected to stimulate local markets by increasing purchasing power, which may in turn boost trade activity and create short-term job opportunities. However, implementation will depend on the confirmation of market functionality to avoid unintended harm to non-beneficiaries. Where feasible, food assistance will be provided in coordination with the Food Security Cluster to ensure alignment with broader humanitarian efforts.ltbrgtThe proposed response plan is designed to remain flexible and responsive to changing needs. Adjustments may be made in coordination with OCHA/SCHF, and pre-positioned funds will only be released upon approval from OCHA and the relevant clusters.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTo maximize impact and avoid duplication of efforts, Violet will actively foster complementarity and coordination with other humanitarian actors. To this end, Violet will ensure proper collaboration with key actors such to jointly address emerging gaps and deliver a harmonized emergency response.ltbrgtFinally, it is worth noting that Violet holds a long-term agreement for FSP, which will be strategically utilized to facilitate rapid deployment under this project.lt/pgt
